problem_statement: The stack provides no way to construct, encode, parse, locate, or validate MAC Length-Type-Value (LTV) elements. A user needs an interface to build LTV headers into a frame buffer, choosing packed or base (unpacked) layout based on the element's type and the cumulative length; to parse LTVs back out of a frame buffer; to validate a whole buffer of LTVs; to search a buffer for an LTV of a given type (advancing or not); and to validate a parsed LTV against a named LTV structure (e.g. a TargetId LTV of type 1 with a minimum length) by type and length. Encoding must handle the special all-zero-length packed form, the escape-mask base format, and report kErrorNoBufs when the buffer is too small, while parsing/validating must report kErrorParse on truncated or otherwise malformed LTVs.
